items.title: The Dedekind-finite tree U_T falls into the definable cardinality class Delta_5
items.author: Supakun Panasawatwong; J. K. Truss
items.difficulty_reason: The theorem is about the set U_T of nodes of a countable weakly 2-transitive tree together with its symmetric model with finite supports, and it pins the definable cardinality of U_T into the class Delta_5, with the sharper negative statement when the tree has infinitely many ramification orders (statement lines 307-308). The proof takes a surjection onto U_T union {*} with finite support A and shows that every point outside the definable closure of A is fixed, by analysing where an image point can sit relative to A: outside the closure the only possible obstruction is a cone at an exceptional ramification point created by a meet with an element of A, and iterating that obstruction for a preimage produces a contradiction (proof lines 310-341). The step that carries the content is the description of the closure [A union {x}] and the two-case analysis built on it, since it is what forces the fixed-point behaviour; surjectivity then fails against the finiteness of the support. H2.
